statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-119377 is an authorizer bypass in SQLite's lookupName(): for a column shared through USING in a RIGHT or FULL JOIN, the sqlite3_set_authorizer() callback was not invoked for every joined table, so SQL can read columns an SQLITE_READ rule denies. SQLite lists it as fixed in 3.54.0: https://sqlite.org/cves.html, https://sqlite.org/bugs/info/2026-07-05T08:15:45Z. The fix is trunk check-in https://sqlite.org/src/info/2cb22877683680c1, mirrored as https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite/commit/5694c3bb2a6a40770ecd2f65910eea756734dfd8, which completes the first fix for this bug, https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite/commit/7ff247c5b9ead3ad8a69c26d3fd264878e127237 (invoke the authorizer on all terms of the USING clause in a RIGHT JOIN); that first fix extends an earlier one for USING columns in a FULL JOIN, https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite/commit/ddea119f825bf07f145c55f623022286bc644664. None of the three trunk commits is in SQLite 3.53.4. DHI's 3.53.4-r1 build is SQLite 3.53.4 with a backport of all three. The DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository publishes packages built from source sqlite (sqlite, sqlite-libs, sqlite-static, sqlite-dev and sqlite-doc) at 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0, 3.53.4-r0 and 3.53.4-r1, for x86_64 and aarch64. We unpacked the sqlite, sqlite-libs, sqlite-static and sqlite-dev packages of every one of those builds on both architectures, each checked against its index checksum. SQLite is compiled into three files in each build: the sqlite3 shell in the sqlite package, which carries its own copy and does not link libsqlite3; the shared library in sqlite-libs; and the static archive libsqlite3.a in sqlite-static. sqlite-dev holds only headers, a pkg-config file and the libsqlite3.so link. The shell and both libraries report SQLite 3.51.1, 3.51.2, 3.53.4 and 3.53.4 in those builds. The 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0 and 3.53.4-r0 builds are built from the upstream 3.51.1, 3.51.2 and 3.53.4 releases, none of which contains the fix. We ran SELECT x FROM t1 FULL JOIN t2 USING(x) with an authorizer that records SQLITE_READ calls, in the sqlite3 shell (.auth on) and in a test program linked once against the shared library and once against the static archive, for every build on x86_64 and aarch64. The SELECT makes no SQLITE_READ authorizer call in 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0 and 3.53.4-r0, and one each for t1.x and t2.x in 3.53.4-r1, on both architectures and in all three copies. The x86_64 runs used Docker Desktop's amd64 emulation. So 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0 and 3.53.4-r0 are affected and 3.53.4-r1 is fixed.
